## 358850: constant additive slack for group-irregular labeling

Exact scope is Conjecture 2.7, arXiv2306.11914v1 p5: one absolute K, every graph with components of order at least three, and EVERY finite abelian group of order at least n+K. The source statement is deliberate; this is not a least-order-only claim. Source pp1–5 definitions, walk operations, Lemmas2.2/2.5 and their proofs, Cor2.3, Th2.4/2.6 and Conj2.7 were read. The exclusion of small even stars enters the actual greedy stock inequality in Lemma2.5, not the walk realization. The source only derives some existence assertions at odd group orders; those cannot by themselves imply the every-order conjecture. The PDF's Figure1 is not visually audited and its two-star examples are not used as new evidence.

Route A: exact incidence-image reduction, all groups, all components.
For a connected bipartite graph with bipartition A,B, prescribed weights w_v can be realized as sums of incident edge labels if and only if sum_A w_v=sum_B w_v. Necessity counts each edge once on either side. Sufficiency: choose a spanning tree and set other labels zero. Remove a leaf v with neighbor u, assign its edge the desired current weight at v and subtract it from the current weight at u. The signed balance is preserved up to deleting the satisfied leaf. At the final root the remaining required weight is zero by balance. Reverse leaf removal to obtain the labels.
For a connected nonbipartite graph, the corresponding condition is sum_v w_v in 2Gamma. Necessity is total weight=2 sum_e label_e. For sufficiency choose a spanning tree, color it A,B, and choose an extra edge with both ends on the same side (an odd cycle guarantees such an edge). Write D=sum_A w-sum_B w. Since D differs from total weight by twice a sum, D is in 2Gamma. If chord ends lie in A, choose x with 2x=D; if in B, choose 2x=-D. Give this chord label x, subtract x from the requirements at its two ends, and the tree requirements are now balanced. Apply the preceding construction. This proof includes torsion and characteristic-two groups and does not assume division by two is unique.
Thus the full conjecture becomes a near-complete injective assignment from Gamma to all vertices with these component constraints. It is still a substantive additive packing problem. Solving each connected component separately does not give disjoint weight sets.

Route B: small-star packets and global stock accounting.
For K1,3, choose distinct leaf weights a,b,c and center d=a+b+c, all four distinct and disjoint from all other packet weights. A union of q such stars asks for q disjoint additive quadruples, with center distinguished. For K1,5 the analogous six distinct weights have the analogous center-sum constraint. In an exponent-two group a four-element zero-sum block works with any center. A two-dimensional subgroup partitions an elementary two-group into cosets of size four; each coset has sum zero (four times its representative plus sum of subgroup), so all such blocks work for K1,3. This is only a parameter family, not the all-group/all-graph theorem and receives no credit.
In general odd-order groups, a complementary triple T={x,y,z}, x+y+z=0 and -T supplies source walk gadgets. The actual source greedily pairs small stars and chooses g avoiding occupied weights. Its inequality |S|>|W|+2 consumes a stock growing with q. Merely tightening that inequality is exactly the one-estimate adaptation that would not qualify even if successful. A genuinely different requirement is a global disjoint packet decomposition into mixed four- and six-element star blocks plus the balanced blocks required by other components, with only O(1) unused group elements uniformly in q and all group structures. No such decomposition is proved here. The source's q-dependent bound does not imply it.

Route C: quotient lifting and orientation transfer.
A quotient Gamma/H can organize packet sums, but selecting a single representative per quotient uses only |Gamma/H| vertices and loses a factor |H| in density. Filling fibers requires simultaneous distinct H-corrections to all packets; the center correction of a star must equal the sum of its leaf corrections, and the demands at a fiber are coupled to other packets. Unpaid lemma: an all-fiber realization with bounded TOTAL leftover, rather than bounded leftover per fiber. An orientation trick also fails: signed directed incidence weights become unsigned weights after changing signs on one bipartition class, but injectivity need not survive, since opposite weights on opposite sides become equal. For nonbipartite components that sign change cannot remove all edge signs at all. The 2026 Cichacz digraph paper is specifically identified by current searches, but its actual theorem/proof was not acquired; the excerpt is navigation, not an authenticated subsumer or a proof of a nonmatch.

Formal feasibility: the literal can be expressed entirely using natural-number encodings of finite graph and finite abelian operation tables, an absolute natural K and an injective weight map. The incidence-image proof also uses only finite graph/tree operations and abelian addition; no real analysis, measure theory, linear algebra or field theory is essential. The missing mixed packet decomposition is the actual mathematical obstruction. No novelty/significance/formal acceptance is asserted.

## 382017: ordered 3-uniform tight paths

Exact source is Bright–Milans–Porter2212.13719v1, Proposition7 and Conjecture13. An edge label phi(uv) in [k] declares an ordered triple u<v<w good when phi(uv)<phi(vw). The maximum number of good triples is ex_<(n,P_(k+2)^(3)). Target bad-triple density is 1/floor((k+1)^2/4), for every fixed k. Source Proposition7 proof, Propositions8/Cor9, Lemmas10–11/Cor12 passages, Conjecture13, the extreme-inversion improvement, Lemmas14–15, Cor16 and Th17 proof were read in text. Final2025EJC124104070 is identified by search, but its full body was not acquired. No final equivalence claim. Material formulas were not visually audited; conclusions below depend only on the text-level exact good-triple reduction, with no figure use.

Route A: coordinate stationarity beyond the source's extreme-label swap.
Fix one edge uv, u<v, and hold all other labels fixed. The only affected good triples have middle u or middle v. The score contribution when its label is l is
F_uv(l)=#{x<u:phi(xu)<l}+#{y>v:l<phi(vy)}.
Consequently F_uv(l+1)-F_uv(l)=#{x<u:phi(xu)=l}-#{y>v:phi(vy)=l+1}.
These exact formulas follow by splitting the two types of triples; the edge uv is never a consecutive edge in a triple with middle strictly between u and v. Hence a globally optimal labeling satisfies F_uv(phi(uv))>=F_uv(l) for every l. This gives all single-edge inequalities, stronger than merely forbidding a k-to-1 extreme inversion. It does NOT show phi(xu)<=phi(uv) at every triple, since the two score terms trade against one another. A change that removes one middle inversion changes many triples at the endpoints, with no uniform sign given by stationarity. Unpaid: a global compression/potential showing existence of a monotone optimum with no greater cost (or a direct density inequality avoiding monotonicity).

Route B: vertex profiles and counting.
Let L_i(v)=#{u<v:phi(uv)=i}, R_j(v)=#{w>v:phi(vw)=j}. Then bad(phi)=sum_v sum_(i>=j) L_i(v)R_j(v), while sum_i L_i(v)=v-1 and sum_j R_j(v)=n-v. Independent optimization of profiles at each v is invalid because one edge uv contributes simultaneously to R_l(u) and L_l(v). Ignoring this edge consistency can artificially put every incoming label low and every outgoing label high at every middle vertex, obtaining zero bad triples. In the monotone case the source builds interval partitions from incoming maxima and outgoing minima; its Lemma15 variations and Th17 control their sizes. Those arguments use monotonicity to certify the changed labeling and to bound destroyed triples. Applying that result unchanged to all optimizers would be circular, not a proof. Need a profile consistency inequality paying the sharp coefficient for arbitrary labels and both parities of k; even-k adjacent-block cross contributions are explicitly unpaid by the source's final discussion.

Route C: finite templates and a counterexample route.
An ordered block template with proportions a_i, labels c_ij between blocks and diagonal labels c_ii has a cubic limiting good-count polynomial. Distinct-block triples contribute a_i a_j a_l for i<j<l exactly when c_ij<c_jl. Two-in-one-block triples contribute a_i^2 a_j/2 or a_i a_j^2/2 according to c_ii<c_ij or c_ij<c_jj. Three-in-one-block triples with a constant diagonal label are bad. Thus any explicit rational template with bad density strictly below 1/floor((k+1)^2/4) would give a full infinite-family negation, after clearing denominators and O(n^2) rounding loss. No such strict template is supplied, no templates were enumerated, and no numerical optimization was done. Vertex-sum monotone templates reproduce the source's construction and cannot count as a new result. Independently assigning uniform labels makes a consecutive pair increasing with probability (k-1)/(2k), far below the source's density for k>=3; random disorder is not a useful refutation mechanism.

Formal feasibility: the original limit notation is real-valued, but the exact assertion admits an equivalent natural-number epsilon formulation. With a=floor((k+1)^2/4), require for all positive q a threshold N such that, for n>=N, the maximal integer good-count differs from (a-1)/a*binom(n,3) by at most binom(n,3)/q, after multiplying by aq. A rational finite template counterexample and all rounding estimates can therefore be stated in natural numbers and finite words/graphs. The literal-to-this-formulation equivalence still must be audited; no Lean endpoint is claimed.

## 350111: full elementary negation of the corrupted literal, zero credit

For k>=2 and global maximum degree one the literal threshold is exactly f(k)=2. To prove every n>=2 works, first select two vertices per part. Add a new pair-edge inside each selected part. Cross edges form a matching and part-edges form another matching. Each component is a path or an even cycle (cycle edges alternate between the two matching types), so a proper two-coloring exists.
